title: Own a pharmacy business only as a pharmacist or a pharmacists' partnership or company
what: Only a pharmacist (or another person the Act allows) may own, or hold an interest in, a pharmacy business.

laws.title: Health Practitioner Regulation (Adoption of National Law) Act 2009 (NSW)
laws.provisions: Health Practitioner Regulation National Law (NSW), Sch 5F cl 5

sources.title: Health Practitioner Regulation (Adoption of National Law) Act 2009 (NSW)
sources.locator: Health Practitioner Regulation National Law (NSW), Sch 5F cl 5(1) (version of 2024-07-01)
sources.quote: (1) A person must not own or otherwise have a financial interest in a pharmacy business (including as a partner or member of a firm) unless as one of the following— (a) a pharmacist; (b) a partner in a pharmacists' partnership; (c) a pharmacists' body corporate or a member of a pharmacists' body corporate. Maximum penalty—100 penalty units.

confidence_note: The law's own words reserve financial interests in pharmacy businesses to pharmacists. Quoted from the Open Australian Legal Corpus copy of the official text, which is not itself official.

assessment.summary: Only pharmacists may own pharmacies, and each may own only a few. It keeps other investors and business models out of community pharmacy; the Harper Review recommended removing the restriction.

marks.reason: Reserves ownership of pharmacies to pharmacists and caps how many each may own: an exclusive right to enter.

assessment.confidence_note: The restriction is explicit; its effect on prices and access has not been measured in Australia. Marks copied from the register item nsw-pharmacy-ownership so the two agree.
